Rashi on Yevamot 8a:11:1.english: Due to her rival wife - Because [the tanna] wanted to teach: "From where [do we derive] her rival wife?"

Rashi on Yevamot 8a:13:1.hebrew: ולקחה לו לאשה ויבמה - המ"ל ולקח אשה וייבם, וכתיב ולקחה — משמע מיעוט: זו ולא אחרת:
Rashi on Yevamot 8a:13:1.english: And take her to him to be his wife and consummate the levirate marriage with her - It could have said: “And take a wife and consummate the levirate marriage,” but it is written: “And take her” — this implies an exclusion: this [woman], and not another.

Rashi on Yevamot 8a:15:1.hebrew: וחד למישרי צרת ערוה שלא במקום מצוה - מרבויא דקרא יתירא דויבמה דרשינן הכי: במקום "ויבמה" הוא דאמינא לך מיעוטא "ולקחה", דמיעט צרה. אבל שלא במקום יבום — כגון צרת בתו מנכרי — שריא:
Rashi on Yevamot 8a:15:1.english: And one to permit the rival wife of a forbidden relation [where it is] not in a place of the mitzvah - From the amplification of the superfluous verse of "and consummate the levirate marriage with her" [ve-yib'mah], we expound thus: It is in a place of ve-yib'mah [where levirate marriage applies] that I told you the exclusion of "and take her" [u-le-kakhah], which excluded a rival wife. However, not in a place of levirate marriage — such as the rival wife of his daughter from an unrelated man — she is permitted.

Rashi on Yevamot 8a:17:1.hebrew: נמי דיקא - כרבא, דערוה פשיטא לן:
Rashi on Yevamot 8a:17:1.english: [The mishna is] also precise - In accordance with Rava, that [the exemption of] a forbidden relation is obvious to us.

Rashi on Yevamot 8a:18:1.hebrew: צרה נמי לא תיבעי - "עליה" קרא לדרשא — דאין עשה דוחה לא תעשה שיש בה כרת, דכתיב "לצרור", דמשמע: לא אחות אשה ולא צרתה, וכתיב כרת בסוף העריות:
Rashi on Yevamot 8a:18:1.english: A rival wife also should not require - [The verse] “with her” [aleha] as a verse for an exposition, for a positive mitzva does not override a prohibition that entails karet — as it is written: “To be a rival” [letzaror], which implies: neither a wife’s sister nor her rival wife; and karet is written at the end of [the section of] forbidden relations.

Rashi on Yevamot 8a:1:1.english: This works out well when the deceased married - This woman first, and she became a brother's wife to this [living brother].

Rashi on Yevamot 8a:1:2.hebrew: ואח"כ נשא חי - את אחותה, וניתוספת איסור אחות אשה על יבמתו. וכשמת אחיו בלא בנים, ואישתראי איסור אשת אח המוקדם — אישתראי נמי אחות אשה המאוחר, כדעולא, דאמר: הואיל והותר לצרעתו שהיא ראשונה, הותר לקריו שהוא אחרון:
Rashi on Yevamot 8a:1:2.english: And afterward the living [brother] married - [He married] her sister, and the prohibition of a wife’s sister was added upon his yevama. And when his brother died without children, and the earlier prohibition of a brother’s wife was permitted, the later [prohibition of] a wife’s sister was also permitted — in accordance with Ulla, who said: Since it was permitted for his leprosy, which was first, it was permitted for his seminal emission, which was last.

Rashi on Yevamot 8a:2:1.hebrew: אלא נשא החי - אשתו תחילה, ועמדה עליו באיסור אחות אשה, ואח"כ נשאה אחיו המת, וניתוסף איסור אשת אח — איסור אחות אשה קדים. ואף על גב דהותר איסור אחרון, עומד ראשון במקומו:
Rashi on Yevamot 8a:2:1.english: Rather, the living [brother] married - His wife first, and [her sister] became forbidden to him under the prohibition of a wife's sister; and afterward his deceased brother married her, and the prohibition of a brother's wife was added — the prohibition of a wife's sister precedes [it]. And even though the latter prohibition is permitted, the first [prohibition] stands in its place.

Rashi on Yevamot 8a:3:1.hebrew: ואפי' נשא מת נמי - ברישא, דקדים ליה איסור אשת אח, לא דמיא לדעולא. דהתם, הרואה קרי בשמיני שלו כבר היה מותר מאיסור הראשון קודם ראיית הקרי, משהאיר המזרח. והכא נמי, תינח היכא דנשא מת ומת תחילה, והותר איסור אשת אח, ואח"כ נשא חי את אחותה:
Rashi on Yevamot 8a:3:1.english: And even if the deceased married as well - In the first clause, where the prohibition of a brother's wife preceded [it], it does not resemble [the case] of Ulla. For there, one who experiences a seminal emission on his eighth [day] was already permitted from the first prohibition prior to experiencing the seminal emission, once the eastern [sky] illuminated. And here too, it works out well [only] where the deceased [brother] married and died first, and the prohibition of a brother's wife was permitted, and afterward the living [brother] married her sister.

Rashi on Yevamot 8a:3:2.hebrew: אלא נשא מת ולא מת - עד שנשא חי את אחותה, הא לא איתחזאי כלל. ומי לא מודה עולא בכהאי גוונא, שאם ראה קרי בליל יום שמיני, שאין מכניס ידיו מחר לבהונות משום קרי דמעכב עליה — הואיל ולא יצא מצרעתו לשעה הראויה להבאת קרבנותיו, דקודם שהותר מצרעתו בא עליו קרי:
Rashi on Yevamot 8a:3:2.english: However, [if] the deceased [brother] married and did not die - [That is, he did not die] until the living [brother] married her sister — behold, she was not fit [for him] at all. And does Ulla not concede in such a case, that if [a leper] experienced a seminal emission on the night of the eighth day, he may not insert his hands tomorrow for [the application to] the thumbs because of the seminal emission that impedes him — since he had not emerged from his leprosy at a time fit for bringing his offerings, for before he was released from his leprosy, a seminal emission came upon him?

Rashi on Yevamot 8a:5:1.hebrew: הכי גרסינן: כי איצטריך עליה — לנשא מת, ומת, ואח"כ נשא חי:
Rashi on Yevamot 8a:5:1.english: This is the reading: When [the phrase] “with her” was necessary — for [the case where] the deceased [brother] married and died, and afterward the living [brother] married.

Rashi on Yevamot 8a:6:1.hebrew: ואיבעית אימא - איצטריך עליה, דאי לא כתביה הוה אמינא: תיתי ייבום אחות אשה להתיר בהיקישא דר' יונה. דאמר רבי יונה: כי כל אשר יעשה מכל התועבות האלה — הוקשו כל העריות זו לזו. ולענין העראה קנסיב ליה ר' יונה בהבא על יבמתו. הכי נמי ה"א: הוקשו כולן לאשת אח, ואע"ג דהכא חד איסורא והכא תרי איסורי — אין משיבין על ההיקש. להכי איצטריך עליה:
Rashi on Yevamot 8a:6:1.english: And if you wish, say - It was necessary [for the verse to write] “with her,” for had it not written it, I would have said: Let the levirate marriage of a wife’s sister be derived to be permitted through the juxtaposition of Rabbi Yona. As Rabbi Yona said: “For whoever shall do any of these abominations” — all forbidden relations were juxtaposed to one another. And regarding the matter of initial intercourse [ha’ara’ah], Rabbi Yona cited it in [the chapter] Haba Al Yevamto. Here too, I would have said: All of them were juxtaposed to a brother’s wife; and even though here [in the case of an ordinary brother’s wife] there is one prohibition, and here [in the case of a wife’s sister] there are two prohibitions — we do not refute a juxtaposition. For this [reason], “with her” was necessary.

Rashi on Yevamot 8a:7:1.english: Since all the forbidden relations - [Those] of our Mishnah.

Rashi on Yevamot 8a:7:2.english: They can be juxtaposed with a brother's wife - To permit levirate marriage.

Rashi on Yevamot 8a:7:3.hebrew: ואיכא לאקושינהו לאחות אשה - דאסירי לייבום, דפרט בה קרא עליה:
Rashi on Yevamot 8a:7:3.english: And they can be juxtaposed with a wife’s sister - That they are forbidden for levirate marriage, for Scripture specified regarding her: “With her.”

Rashi on Yevamot 8a:7:4.hebrew: מאי חזית דאקשת להו לאחות אשה - כדקתני בריש פרקין: מה אחות אשה מיוחדת כו':
Rashi on Yevamot 8a:7:4.english: What did you see that you juxtaposed them with a wife’s sister - As was taught at the beginning of our chapter: “Just as a wife’s sister is unique...”, etc.

Tosafot on Yevamot 8a:17:1.hebrew: ואילו פטורות ופוטרות לא קתני - אע"ג דמסקינן דלאסור צרתה נמי לא צריך קרא, מ"מ תנא פוטרות — דהוצרך להשמיענו איסור בצרה, שעדיין לא השמיענו בשום מקום. אבל איסור ערוה — דכבר נשנו כל העריות בפרק קמא דכריתות (דף ב.) — שלא איצטריך כאן להשמיענו דאסורה במקום מצוה, דפשיטא דאין עשה דוחה ל"ת שיש בו כרת:
Tosafot on Yevamot 8a:17:1.english: Whereas "are exempt and exempt others" is not taught - Even though we conclude that prohibiting her rival wife also does not require a verse, nevertheless, [the Tanna] taught "exempt" [their rival wives] — for he needed to teach us a prohibition regarding a rival wife, which he had not yet taught us anywhere. However, regarding the prohibition of a forbidden relation — since all the forbidden relations were already taught in the first chapter of Keritot (2a) — it was not necessary to teach us here that she is forbidden where the mitzvah applies, for it is obvious that a positive commandment does not override a negative commandment that entails karet.

Tosafot on Yevamot 8a:4:1.hebrew: מי לא מודה עולא בהא שאם ראה קרי בליל שמיני שאין מכניס ידיו לבהונות - ק"ק: דמנא ליה דמודה עולא בהא? וגם בפרק כל הפסולים (זבחים לב: ושם), דמהדר עולא למאן דפריך ליה מהך ברייתא: "ומטונך, דמצורע הואיל והותר לצרעתו כו'" — דמשמע: "ומטונך" — ממשא שאתה בא להכביד עליו אביא ראייתי משם, ומה ראיה יש לו מן הברייתא? ונראה לרבינו יצחק, דדייק עולא מדנקט: "וראה קרי בו ביום" — משמע: בו ביום, אבל בלילה לא; שמע מינה דטעמא משום דהותר לצרעתו הותר נמי לקריו. ולהכי פשיטא ליה הכא דמודי עולא בראה קרי בליל ח':
Tosafot on Yevamot 8a:4:1.english: "Doesn’t Ulla agree in this [case], that if he experienced a seminal emission on the night of the eighth, that he does not insert his hands to the thumbs" - It is somewhat difficult: From where does [the Gemara] know that Ulla agrees to this? And also, in the chapter [entitled] Kol HaPesulim (Zevachim 32b, and there), where Ulla responds to the one who raises an objection against him from this baraita: "[A proof may be brought] from your [own] burden: A leper [is different], since he was permitted for his leprosy, etc.," which implies: "From your burden" — from the load with which you come to burden him, I will bring my proof from there. But what proof does he have from the baraita? And it appears to Rabbeinu Yitzchak that Ulla deduced [it] from [the fact] that [the baraita] stated: "and he experienced a seminal emission on that [same] day" — which implies: on that day, but at night, no; deduce from this that the reason is that since he was permitted for his leprosy, he was also permitted for his emission. And therefore, it was obvious to [the Gemara] here that Ulla agrees in [the case of one who] experienced a seminal emission on the night of the eighth [that he may not insert his hands].

Tosafot on Yevamot 8a:8:1.hebrew: תרי איסורי [מחד איסורא לא ילפינן] - (אבל שלא במקום ייבום, כגון צרת בתו — ילפי'). וא"ת: ולרב אסי, אמאי פוטרת איילונית צרתה? והא חד איסורא הוא! וי"ל: דממה נפשך איהי אסירא, דילפי' מ"אשר תלד" — פרט לאיילונית, ולהכי צרתה נמי אסורה; וכן אשת אחיו שלא היה בעולמו. אבל קשיא: מאי טעמא דמאן דפליג אדרב אסי? וי"ל: דכיון דאיילונית לאו בת ייבום היא בשום מקום, חשיבא צרתה כצרת ערוה שלא במקום מצוה — דשריא. ולא דמיא איילונית לחייבי עשה, דילפינן בפרק שני (לקמן יבמות דף כ.) לחליצה; דאיילונית, מיעטה הכתוב בהדיא, דלא הויא בכלל היתר אשת אח:
Tosafot on Yevamot 8a:8:1.english: "Two prohibitions [we do not derive from one prohibition]" - (However, not in the context of levirate marriage, such as the co-wife of his daughter, we do derive [it]). And if you will say: And according to Rav Assi, why does an aylonit exempt her co-wife? But isn't it [only] one prohibition?! And one can say: Whichever way you look at it, she herself is forbidden, as we derive from: "[the firstborn] that she bears" — excluding an aylonit; and therefore, her co-wife is also forbidden. And likewise [in the case of] the wife of his brother who was not in his lifetime. However, it is difficult: What is the reasoning of the one who disagrees with Rav Assi? And one can say: Since an aylonit is not eligible for levirate marriage under any circumstances, her co-wife is considered like the co-wife of a forbidden relation not in the context of the mitzvah — who is permitted. And an aylonit is not comparable to those [forbidden by] a positive commandment, regarding whom we derive in the second chapter (below, Yevamot 20a) [that they require] ḥalitza; because [in the case of] an aylonit, Scripture explicitly excluded her, so that she was never included in the permission of a brother's wife.

Tosafot on Yevamot 8a:9:1.hebrew: רבא אמר ערוה גופה לא צריכא קרא - וא"ת: והא לכל הפחות איצטריך לינשא מת, ומת, ואח"כ נשא חי — דלא תימא: "הואיל ואישתרי אשתרי"? וי"ל: דרבא לית ליה דעולא, וסבר דביאה במקצת לא שמה ביאה. ועוד, אר"י דיש לחלק: דגבי בעל קרי, דשם טומאה אחת היא, אמרי' "הואיל ואשתרי אישתרי", דחד לאו הוא בבעל קרי ומצורע; אבל הכא, דשני שמות הן, לא אמרינן "הואיל ואישתרי אישתרי". וא"ת: מאי טעמא לא צריכא קרא? וכי לית ליה לרבא היקישא דרבי יונה? וי"ל: דקסבר דלענין איסורא הוא דאקשינהו רחמנא, דבהכי איירי קרא, ולא לענין היתירא:
Tosafot on Yevamot 8a:9:1.english: "Rava said: A forbidden relation herself does not require a verse" - And if you say: But surely at the very least [a verse] was necessary for [the case where] the deceased [brother] married [her] and died, and afterward the living [brother] married [her sister] — so that you should not say: "Since it was permitted, it is permitted"? And one can say that Rava does not accept [the view] of Ulla, and maintains that partial entry is not considered entry. And furthermore, the Ri said that one can distinguish: for in the case of one who experienced a seminal emission, where it is a single category of ritual impurity, we say: "Since it was permitted, it is permitted," as it is a single negative prohibition regarding [both] one who experienced a seminal emission and a leper; but here, where they are two [distinct] categories, we do not say: "Since it was permitted, it is permitted." And if you say: What is the reason [that a forbidden relation herself] does not require a verse? Does Rava not accept the juxtaposition of Rabbi Yona? And one can say that [Rava] maintains that it is [only] with regard to prohibition that the Merciful One juxtaposed them, for that is what the verse is dealing with, and not with regard to permission.

Tosafot on Yevamot 8a:9:2.hebrew: כי איצטריך קרא למיסר צרה - ותימה: דהיכי טעי למימר דאיצטריך למיסר צרה טפי מן הערוה, כיון דצרה מלצרור נפקא, ויש כרת בצרה כמו בערוה?! ואומר רבינו יצחק, דהשתא נמי בעי למימר: לאיסור צרה, ולמידק דשלא במקום מצוה שריא — כדמסיק רב אחא לבסוף. והא דקאמר נמי: "אין לי אלא היא — משום צרתה", לא משום דצריך קרא לאיסור, אלא למידק היתירא שלא במקום מצוה. והא דפריך: "מאי שנא ערוה דלא צריכא קרא כו'" — גמרא טעי במילתיה דרבא, שלא פירש בהדיא: למישרי שלא במקום מצוה אתא עליה:
Tosafot on Yevamot 8a:9:2.english: "When the verse was necessary, [it was] to prohibit a rival wife" - And it is puzzling: How could [one] mistakenly say that [the verse] was necessary to prohibit a rival wife more than the forbidden relation [herself], since [the prohibition of] a rival wife is derived from “to be a rival” [letzror, Leviticus 18:18], and there is karet for a rival wife just as for a forbidden relation?! And Rabbeinu Yitzchak says that now too he meant to say: [The verse was necessary] for the prohibition of a rival wife, and to infer that [when] not in the context of a mitzvah she is permitted — as Rav Aḥa concludes in the end. And that which [the Gemara] also says: “I have only her — [stated] on account of her rival wife,” [this is] not because a verse is needed for the prohibition, but rather to infer the permission [of a rival wife] when not in the context of a mitzvah. And as for that which [the Gemara] challenges: “What is different about a forbidden relation that she does not require a verse, etc.?” — the Gemara erred in [understanding] Rava’s statement, because he had not explicitly explained that [the word] “aleha” [“with her”] comes to permit [a rival wife] when not in the context of a mitzvah.
